findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", giving the user near-administrative control over compute, storage, serverless and monitoring in the account. This violates least privilege and creates a broad privilege-escalation and data-exfiltration path (e.g. s3:* allows reading every bucket, lambda:*/ec2:* allows running code with attached roles).

A permanent IAM access key is provisioned for a human-style IAM user instead of using federation/role assumption with temporary credentials. The key never expires unless manually rotated and, combined with the wildcard user policy, compromise of the key yields near-admin account access.

No pgp_key is supplied, so the generated secret access key is stored unencrypted in the Terraform state file, exposing a live credential to anyone able to read state (often a shared S3 backend or CI artifact).

The root module output "secret" exports the access key secret attribute, which is written to state and printed/consumable by any caller of the module or CI pipeline, widening the audience for a long-lived credential.

Permissions are granted directly to an IAM user via an inline policy rather than through a group or assumable role, making the highly privileged access permanent and hard to audit or revoke centrally; no permissions boundary is set to cap what the user can do.
